newsitem.title: USA: Wall St stocks close broadly higher, Dow rises 83.
newsitem.headline: Wall St stocks close broadly higher, Dow rises 83.

text.p: U.S. stocks staged a broad rally Thursday, as blue chips continued to reverse the damage from their recent sell-off and investors got new evidence that business trends remain robust in the technology sector.
The Dow industrials gained 83 points to close unofficially at 6824, putting the average back within reach of its all-time closing high of 6883.90, set on January 21.
As on that session, markets today waited and watched as Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan briefed a congressional committee on the state of the U.S. economy.
Then, as today, Greenspan gave little hint that the Fed was considering raising interest rates at the central bank's policy meeting next week.
"I still picture them as trigger-finger ready but I don't think it will happen next week," said Allen Sinai, chief global economist at Primark Decision Economics.

With most on Wall Street convinced rate policy will be steady for the foreseeable future -- after next week, the Fed is not scheduled to meet again until the end of March -- markets found themselves cleared to advance.
"If the Fed doesn't raise rates, then there's still upside," said Edgar Peters, chief investment strategist at PanAgora Asset Management Inc.

Over the last two days the Dow has recouped some two-thirds of what it lost during its five day mini-slide. Peters said the pullback might actually be a sign the market is behaving in a more healthy fashion than in recent years.
"The market rose very fast and that was a little crazy," he said. "You have to expect some pullbacks. The thing that's been unhealthy is the lack of pullbacks over the last year or two."
Semiconductor companies were among the strongest performers today, boosted by Intel Corp's decision to hold prices for its high end Pentium Pro chips essentially steady in the first quarter.
Analysts had expected Intel to cut prices to some degree from fourth quarter levels and took the news as evidence that demand remains strong for the chips.
"The underlying tone is that it's not over in tech-land yet," said Arnie Owen, director of equities at Kaufman Brothers.

Intel shares surged 5-3/8 to 160-1/8 and others in the sector followed suit. Micron Technology Inc climbed 2-1/4 to 35-1/4 and semiconductor equipment maker Applied Materials Inc gained 2-1/2 to 48-3/8.

The news was a mixed blessing for the technology universe, however. Largely left out of the rally were personal computer makers, which are the main buyers of microprocessors and therefore stand to lose from the firm pricing levels.
Gateway 2000 Inc gained 1/4 to 60-1/4 and Dell Computer Corp rose 3/8 to 66.
Drug stocks remained firm, as investors flocked to the group's solid earnings and defensive appeal.
Warner-Lambert Co jumped 3-1/8 to 78 after announcing the U.S. Food and Drug Administration had approved its Rezulin anti-diabetes tablets.
Other pharmaceutical standouts included Eli Lilly & Co, which gained 4-7/8 to 86-7/8, and Pfizer Inc, up 4-1/8 to 90-3/4.
Procter & Gamble Co added 3-57/64 to 115-1/8 to lead all Dow components. Since reporting earnings Tuesday morning, P&G shares have risen more than seven points.
In other individual issues, Hughes Supply Inc tumbled 5-1/8 to 33-1/4 after warning that its fourth-quarter earnings would fall short of Wall Street estimates.
Jayhawk Acceptance Corp skidded 4-1/2 to 3-5/8 after reporting a fourth-quarter loss. The company cited a $15.5 million charge to increase its credit loss allowance.

Mercury Finance Co failed to open for trading for the second straight session since it disclosed discovering accounting irregularities that had resulted in earnings overstatements totalling $90 million over the last four years.
The S&P 500 rose 11.67 to 784.17.
The Nasdaq Composite gained 15.85 to 1371.02.
The Russell 2000 small-cap index rose 2.04 to 368.29.
(Figures official as of 1645 EST/2145 GMT).
((-- Wall Street desk 212 859 1721))
